findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define how a tidy:<class> whose tickets are discarded or never closed counts toward the per-class shortfall brake, so a class that structurally fails to land is not re-proposed forever.
evidence: Plan: the opening step 'compares each closed tidy:<class> ticket's merged diff to its declaration, comments any shortfall on that ticket, and counts shortfalls per class'
A tidy ticket that is never closed (or whose discovery plan was discarded at the 24h window) produces no merged diff and therefore no shortfall comment
Plan: 'a class with two is not re-proposed' is the only re-proposal brake
findings.finding: The shortfall-counting corrective loop only inspects CLOSED tidy:<class> tickets, so a class whose plans are repeatedly discarded under the 24-hour window (or whose tickets are abandoned without closing) never accrues a shortfall and is re-proposed indefinitely — the 'a class with two is not re-proposed' brake never engages for the failure mode of never-landing.
findings.location: 'The change' bullet 'the measuring actor is therefore the next run … compares each closed tidy:<class> ticket's merged diff to its declaration … counts shortfalls per class'
scenarios: A tidy:<class> whose condensations keep failing review and never merge is re-discovered and re-proposed every run, burning the 5-ticket cap on a class that structurally cannot land
findings.suggested_fix: Count a discarded/abandoned tidy:<class> ticket (closed-without-merge, or plan discarded at the 24h window) as a shortfall for that class, so the 'two shortfalls → not re-proposed' brake also catches classes that never land.

findings.checklist_item: Enumerate the admissible tidy:<class> values (the fixed set of change classes), or state the rule that derives a class from the retired-mechanism kind, so the two-strike shortfall count is deterministic.
evidence: Plan: 'each ticket it files carries a `tidy:<class>` tag naming its change class'
Plan: 'counts shortfalls per class by searching the tag; a class with two is not re-proposed. No new store — the count IS those comments'

The corrective rule 'a class with two is not re-proposed' is only enforceable if the class set is a fixed, known vocabulary; a free-form string lets an executor rename a class to evade the two-strike count
A referenced schema/enum whose value vocabulary is never defined is a MAJOR T8 gap
findings.finding: The tidy:<class> tag is used as the schema key for the entire shortfall/two-strike corrective loop, but the plan never defines the value vocabulary of <class> (the admissible change classes).
findings.location: The change — modify, not discard; AC line 'A change class is a tidy:<class> tag...'
scenarios: An executor files two shortfall tickets under slightly different class spellings and neither crosses the two-strike threshold
The next run cannot deterministically search the tag because it does not know which class values exist
findings.suggested_fix: Define tidy:<class> as a closed enum — e.g. one class per mechanism kind the ratchet counts (lock, env_var, config_key, feature_flag, ci_gate, autouse_fixture, test_helper) plus a 'loc' class for pure line deletions — and state that the next run searches exactly those tag values.

findings.checklist_item: Define how non-merged closed tickets and still-open tickets contribute to the per-class shortfall count (e.g. closed-without-merge counts as a full shortfall; still-open tickets are not yet measured).
evidence: Plan: 'the same opening step compares each closed tidy:<class> ticket's merged diff to its declaration, comments any shortfall on that ticket, and counts shortfalls per class'
A ticket can be closed without a merged diff, or remain open across the 24h window / the next run; the plan treats 'closed' and 'has a merged diff' as equivalent
Ambiguous counter/state-increment placement and missing fallback for an incomplete sub-step are T8 checklist items
findings.finding: The shortfall counter increments by comparing 'each closed tidy:<class> ticket's merged diff to its declaration', but the plan does not define how a tidy ticket that was closed without a merge (rejected/won't-do), has no merged diff, or is still open at next-run time contributes to the per-class shortfall tally.
findings.location: The change — modify, not discard; AC line 'shortfalls are counted by searching that tag'
scenarios: A tidy ticket is rejected and closed with no merge — does it count as a shortfall for its class?
A tidy ticket is still open when the next run's opening step runs — is it measured, deferred, or counted?

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name (or specify the creation of) the test that asserts neither skill names a specific model/vendor, with the concrete pattern/paths it scans.
evidence: Plan: 'Neither skill names a specific model or vendor. Verified by a test.'

The three named proving commands (check_skill_frontmatter, test_janitor_concern_schema, test_skill_shared_sync) validate frontmatter, concern-list contiguity and shared-sync — none assert absence of a model/vendor name.
No step describes creating a provider-neutrality test.
findings.finding: The final acceptance criterion 'Neither skill names a specific model or vendor. Verified by a test.' asserts a proving test but does not name the test or state whether it must be authored; the three tests the grounding section does name (test_janitor_concern_schema, test_skill_shared_sync, check_skill_frontmatter) do not check vendor-neutrality.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria, last bullet: 'Verified by a test.'
scenarios: An executor marks the AC met by inspection but no CI test exists to catch a future vendor-specific string regressing into either SKILL.md.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a step creating e.g. tests/unit/test_skill_provider_neutral.py that greps both SKILL.md trees for a denylist of vendor/model tokens and asserts none match, and cite it in the AC.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the shortfall comment idempotent — key each shortfall comment to its (ticket, measurement SHA) so a re-run of the opening/measuring step does not double-count a single shortfall when searching the tag.
evidence: Plan: 'comments any shortfall on that ticket, and counts shortfalls per class by searching the tag; a class with two is not re-proposed. No new store — the count IS those comments'
A comment-as-count store with no dedup key is sensitive to re-execution: two runs (or one retried run) measuring the same closed ticket append two shortfall comments for one shortfall
findings.finding: The corrective loop uses ticket comments as the shortfall store ('No new store — the count IS those comments') but specifies no idempotency key tying a shortfall comment to a specific (ticket, measurement SHA). If the opening/measuring step runs more than once against the same closed ticket — a retried, resumed, or re-invoked run — it re-comments the same shortfall, and the tag-search count double-counts, tripping the 'two → not re-proposed' brake on a single real shortfall.
findings.location: 'The change' bullet: 'the same opening step … comments any shortfall on that ticket, and counts shortfalls per class by searching the tag … No new store — the count IS those comments'
scenarios: A tidying run is interrupted after commenting a shortfall and re-run; the second pass re-comments, and a class with one genuine shortfall now reads as two and is wrongly retired from re-proposal
findings.suggested_fix: Require each shortfall comment to carry the measured SHA and the ticket id, and have the opening step skip tickets that already bear a shortfall comment for the SHA it is measuring, so the tag-search count is stable under re-execution.

findings.checklist_item: Specify the first-run fallback: when no previous-run SHA exists, state that the opening step records the discovery SHA as the baseline and emits no realized-delta result.
evidence: Plan: 'the NEXT run opens by measuring main's LOC and mechanism count against the SHA the previous run recorded'
Plan: 'the measuring actor is therefore the next run'
No first-run / bootstrap case is described — a fallback for an incomplete/missing prior sub-step is an explicit T8 checklist item
findings.finding: The success metric and corrective loop both depend on 'the SHA the previous run recorded', but the plan specifies no behavior for the first run, which has no previous-run SHA to measure against.
findings.location: The change — modify, not discard; AC line 'Its success metric is the realized delta on main...'
scenarios: The first-ever rebar-tidy run reaches its opening step and finds no recorded prior SHA

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the RETIRE/reset path for the shortfall count: whether a tidy:<class> blocked at two shortfalls is permanent or can be cleared, and how (e.g. an operator override, a time/SHA window, or a resolving comment that the tag search excludes).
evidence: 'the same opening step compares each closed tidy:<class> ticket's merged diff to its declaration, comments any shortfall on that ticket, and counts shortfalls per class by searching the tag; a class with two is not re-proposed. No new store — the count IS those comments'

ABSENCE: the plan defines who creates the shortfall comment (the next run) and who consumes it (the tag search), but never states a retirement/reset path — whether a class stays permanently blocked, or how the count is cleared once remediable.
findings.finding: The shortfall-count state (ticket comments on tidy:<class> tickets) has a defined create and consume path but no RETIRE/reset path: a class that accumulates two shortfalls 'is not re-proposed' permanently, and the comments accumulate indefinitely with no stated way to clear a class after the underlying obstacle is resolved.
findings.location: The change — modify, not discard: 'No new store — the count IS those comments' / 'a class with two is not re-proposed'
scenarios: A tidy:<class> whose two shortfalls were caused by a transient obstacle (e.g. a later-reverted conflicting change) is permanently excluded from re-proposal because searching the tag still finds two shortfall comments.
Over many runs, shortfall comments accumulate on historical tickets with no bound, and the 'count by searching the tag' grows monotonically.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to the corrective-loop bullet defining reset: e.g. 'a class reaching two shortfalls is suppressed until an operator posts a clearing comment (or the blocking condition's ticket is reopened), which the tag search treats as zeroing the count.'

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Scope the 'realized delta' success metric to the janitor's own merged tidy:<class> diffs (reconcile it with the per-ticket merged-diff comparison), rather than the raw LOC/mechanism delta of main between two SHAs which also absorbs feature and defect-audit work.
evidence: Plan: 'the NEXT run opens by measuring main's LOC and mechanism count against the SHA the previous run recorded, and that realized delta is the previous run's result'
Plan (same section): the corrective loop 'compares each closed tidy:<class> ticket's merged diff to its declaration' — a per-diff measure, not a whole-main diff
Between two SHAs main also absorbs the defect-audit's remediations and feature work, which the whole-main delta would silently credit/debit to the janitor
findings.finding: The headline success metric — 'realized delta on main, LOC and mechanism count measured against the previous run's recorded SHA' — attributes the entire main-to-main delta to the janitor, but features, defect-audit remediations, and unrelated commits also move LOC and mechanism count between the two SHAs. The plan elsewhere specifies a correctly-scoped per-ticket measurement (comparing each closed tidy ticket's MERGED DIFF to its declaration), so the two measurement definitions conflict: one is whole-main, one is per-diff.
findings.location: 'The change' bullet 'a run is scored by what LANDED' and AC 'Its success metric is the realized delta on main'
scenarios: A feature adds 300 LOC between janitor runs; the janitor deleted 200 LOC but the main-delta shows +100, scoring a successful tidy run as a failure
A concurrent defect-audit remediation retires a mechanism; the janitor is credited for a retirement it did not cause
findings.suggested_fix: State that the realized delta is the SUM over the previous run's closed tidy:<class> tickets of (lines removed, mechanisms retired) in each ticket's merged diff — the same per-ticket measurement the corrective loop already uses — not the whole-main LOC/mechanism delta between the two recorded SHAs.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State explicitly which skill retains the 'never edits code' rule, and clarify whether the tidy janitor performs deletions directly or files deletion tickets (reconciling the ticket-cap/merged-diff language with gap critique #2).
evidence: Grounding: the three 'Never edits code' statements (SKILL.md:14,:68,:127) 'all three move with the split' — but the plan never states to WHICH skill they move.
Gap #2: '"Never edits code" turns tidying into ticket generation. 20 to 37 tickets per run enter the same pipeline that produces the complexity.'

Contract bullets: 'a run is capped at 5 tickets', 'each ticket it files carries a tidy:<class> tag', 'compares each closed tidy:<class> ticket's merged diff to its declaration' — all presuppose the tidy janitor still files tickets.
findings.finding: The plan does not resolve which skill keeps the 'never edits code' rule, and the tidy janitor's contract is internally ambiguous about whether it makes deletions directly or files tickets for others to land. The gap critique (#2) says 'never edits code turns tidying into ticket generation,' implying the tidy janitor should stop generating tickets — yet its own ACs reference 'ticket cap of 5', 'each ticket it files', and comparing 'its merged diff to its declaration', which describe a ticket-filing skill.
findings.location: 'The change' section + grounding note on the three 'Never edits code' statements
scenarios: An executor cannot tell whether the tidy janitor's 'admissible outputs are deletions and collapses' means it performs the deletions or files deletion tickets; and cannot tell whether 'never edits code' applies to it, the defect audit, or both.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence: e.g. 'The defect audit retains never-edits-code (it files tickets). The tidy janitor files deletion tickets too, but is scored on realized merged deletions; its ticket cap and tidy:<class> tags presuppose ticket-filing.' — or, if it edits directly, say so and drop the ticket language.
